title: Agent Regression Testing: Pre-Release Evaluation vs Production Signals

steps.prompt: An architect is changing the instructions and action inputs of a live Agentforce service agent with 12 topics. The change must not alter how any topic classifies requests or which actions it calls, and the agent's reply wording varies from run to run. How should the team test for regressions?

options.label: Run a sandbox batch test on all 12 topics, scoring topic and action choices
options.rationale: Agent tests check behavior against expected outcomes rather than one exact output, and end-to-end tests exist to show performance does not degrade as changes are made. Unchanged topics need coverage too, because edited instructions can shift classification anywhere in the agent.

options.label: Chat with the agent in a sandbox using a few prompts for each changed topic
options.rationale: A handful of hand-typed prompts covers only the topics the team expects to change and cannot be rerun the same way, so shifts in the other topics go unseen.

options.label: Release behind a feature flag to 5% of users and compare their error rates
options.rationale: The canary still lets real customers find the regression, and a misrouted topic or wrong action usually returns no error, so error rates miss it.

options.label: Rerun saved prompts and require each reply to match the pre-change response text
options.rationale: Reply wording varies between runs, so exact-match assertions fail on correct answers and the suite's failures stop signaling real regressions.
